keeps the secret completely and shares his own lunch with his friend every day
announces to the whole class that they should all help his friend get food
tells only the form teacher without considering his friend's feelings about his dignity
payload.explanation: A counsellor can arrange free meals discreetly, protecting both the friend's dignity and their wellbeing.

payload.snippet: Nina is halfway through her lunch when a classmate sits down and tells her they were very sick last week after eating the exact same food Nina is currently eating.
options: stops eating immediately and tells a teacher so the food can be checked safely
continues eating since she has eaten it many times before without any problems
shares this alarming information with the entire class as a warning right away
throws all her food away and goes to look for something safer to eat
payload.explanation: Stopping and alerting a teacher so the food can be properly checked protects the safety of everyone.

payload.snippet: Tom witnesses a kitchen staff member accept money from a popular student and give that student extra food portions while other hungry students who need more food are being turned away.
options: reports what he saw honestly to the head teacher or a trusted senior staff member
ignores it since the staff member is an adult and presumably knows best
tells the student who paid that what they did was completely unfair
collects money from his friends so they can also pay for extra food the same way
payload.explanation: Reporting this to a senior staff member addresses the unfairness and protects all students equally.

payload.snippet: Ava is in the lunch queue when she notices the student directly ahead of her is beginning to have an allergic reaction — hives appearing rapidly on their neck — and the student does not seem to realise what is happening to them.
options: alerts a teacher immediately and stays calmly with the affected student
waits a few minutes to see whether the hives might go away on their own
tells her friends behind her in the queue to come and look at what is happening
asks the student directly whether they feel okay and waits for their response
payload.explanation: An allergic reaction can escalate extremely quickly — alerting a teacher immediately could save a life.

payload.snippet: Ben finds a handwritten note tucked inside his lunchbox suggesting his food has been tampered with and that he should not eat it, but he cannot tell if it is a genuine warning or just a prank from a classmate.
options: does not eat the food and shows the note immediately to a teacher
reads the note, decides it is almost certainly a prank, and eats the food anyway
throws both the note and all the food away carefully without telling anyone at all
shows the note to his closest friends and asks them to help him decide what to do
payload.explanation: Not eating the food and showing the note to a teacher is the safest response — it could be a genuine warning.

payload.snippet: Grace realises that the food labelling in the school cafeteria has a significant error today that could badly affect anyone with a dairy allergy, and she only knows this because she reads all labels carefully for her own intolerance.
options: tells a cafeteria supervisor about the labelling error immediately and clearly
makes a mental note to mention it to her parents later that same evening
warns only the specific students she personally knows have dairy intolerances
posts about the error on the school social media group to warn all students herself
payload.explanation: Telling the cafeteria supervisor immediately is the action most likely to prevent serious harm to students today.

payload.snippet: Max is selected to represent his whole class in a prestigious lunch competition, but he finds out moments before it starts that the prize involves eating a food that directly conflicts with his religious dietary rules.
options: politely withdraws from the competition and explains his dietary rules clearly to the organiser
eats the food just this once to avoid letting his entire class down
pretends to eat the food during the competition but secretly hides it without swallowing
competes and wins first place but refuses the prize without giving any explanation at all
payload.explanation: Politely withdrawing and explaining dietary rules is honest, respectful, and protects his religious beliefs.

payload.snippet: Lily overhears a group of girls at the lunch table making a deliberate plan to tell the new student that there is no room to sit when there clearly is, just to exclude her because she looks different from the group.
options: tells the girls their plan is unkind and invites the new student to sit with her herself
stays completely quiet so as not to risk falling out with her friend group
goes along with the exclusion plan in order to remain accepted by the group
tells a teacher about the plan without first making any effort to resolve it herself
payload.explanation: Standing up for the new student and personally inviting her is both brave and the right thing to do.

payload.snippet: Zoe discovers that a classmate who very publicly and loudly shames others for eating unhealthy food has been secretly throwing their own healthy packed lunches in the bin every day and buying sweets from the corner shop instead.
options: stays quiet since it is their private business, but does not join in any of the public shaming
tells the whole class publicly about the hypocrisy she has discovered
confronts the classmate directly in front of the entire lunch group about it
tells a teacher about the discarded healthy food as a food waste concern
payload.explanation: Keeping private behaviour private while not joining unkind public shaming shows both discretion and integrity.

payload.snippet: Sam is asked by the school journalist to comment on the quality of cafeteria food for the school newsletter, but he knows his completely honest opinion will genuinely upset the cafeteria staff he likes very much as people.
options: gives an honest but carefully constructive and politely worded comment about the food
says the food is absolutely wonderful even though he sincerely does not believe it
declines to comment at all since he does not want to hurt anyone's feelings
gives a very harsh and extremely critical review without any consideration for the staff
payload.explanation: Honest, constructive feedback helps improve things over time without being unkind to the people involved.

payload.snippet: Finn's best friend asks him to back up a false story that a particular child spilled something on them intentionally, so they can get that child punished by a teacher, but Finn clearly saw it was a complete accident.
options: refuses to lie and tells the teacher honestly what he actually witnessed
agrees to back up his friend's false story in order to be loyal to him
stays completely silent and leaves the teacher to figure out the truth alone
tells his friend to come clean himself, saying he will speak up if the friend does not
payload.explanation: Refusing to lie and telling the truth protects an innocent person from unfair punishment.

payload.snippet: Ruby notices through consistent observation that her school's lunch programme has been giving noticeably smaller food portions to students from lower-income families who receive free meals compared to those who pay the full price.
options: raises this serious fairness concern with a trusted teacher or school council representative
says nothing since the issue does not directly affect her own lunch at all
starts quietly moving food from her own tray to give to the students getting less
takes photographs as evidence of the unfair portions to post online straightaway
payload.explanation: Raising a systemic fairness concern through appropriate school channels is the responsible and most impactful action.

payload.snippet: Owen is finishing his lunch when he clearly witnesses a cafeteria staff member pocket the change from a student who paid with a note and then walk away quickly without giving the correct change back.
options: tells the head teacher or a senior staff member honestly about what he just witnessed
says nothing since the staff member probably just made an honest mistake
tells the student directly to go back and firmly ask for their change immediately
tells only his close friends privately so they know to watch their own change carefully
payload.explanation: Reporting witnessed financial dishonesty to a senior person in authority is the honest and correct action.

payload.snippet: Sophie's closest friend has been dieting in an increasingly obsessive way and has become visibly very thin, but Sophie knows her friend becomes extremely angry and upset if anyone ever mentions food or eating habits to her face.
options: tells a school counsellor or trusted teacher about her concerns privately and carefully
respects her friend's complete autonomy and decides to say absolutely nothing about it
tries to encourage her friend to eat more by making lighthearted jokes about the food
tells her friend directly and bluntly one day that she urgently needs to eat more
payload.explanation: Sharing concerns about a friend's health with a professional is the most responsible action, even when the situation feels difficult.

payload.snippet: Jake discovers that someone at school has been secretly taking photographs of students eating lunch and posting them online with mocking captions about people's food choices, all without the subjects' knowledge or permission.
options: reports this to a teacher and provides any evidence he has access to
directly warns the students being photographed so they can defend themselves online
posts a counter-response online to publicly defend all the students being mocked
waits passively to see whether the person responsible eventually gets caught themselves
payload.explanation: Reporting to a teacher with evidence is the appropriate way to address online bullying that originates at school.

payload.snippet: Chloe is sitting at the lunch table when another student suddenly begins acting confused and disoriented — and Chloe knows this student has type one diabetes and may urgently need sugar right now.
options: finds a teacher or the school nurse immediately and tells them the student needs help now
gives the student a sweet from her own lunchbox and then waits to see if it helps
asks the student directly what they need and patiently waits for a coherent answer
goes to get several more friends to help assess the situation before finding a teacher
payload.explanation: A diabetic hypoglycaemic episode is a genuine medical emergency — finding trained help immediately is absolutely vital.

payload.snippet: Ethan is selected by a teacher to serve as the official class lunch monitor and discovers that the most popular child in the year has been receiving double the dessert allocation every day by charming a particular kitchen assistant with compliments.
options: reports the situation honestly to the supervising teacher
ignores it entirely since the popular student might make his life very difficult if he reports it
starts quietly accepting extra dessert himself since the system is already clearly unfair
confronts the kitchen assistant directly about their personal role in the unfair arrangement
payload.explanation: Reporting the situation to the supervising teacher is honest and upholds fair rules for every student.

payload.snippet: Isla finds out through a group chat that a coordinated plan to waste as much food as possible and throw packed lunches away is being quietly organised by students who want to protest about the poor quality of cafeteria food.
options: suggests the group write a formal petition or speak to the student council instead of wasting food
joins the food-throwing protest since the cafeteria food genuinely does need to get better
reports the plan directly to a teacher so it can be stopped before it starts
starts a counter-movement campaign to make sure all students continue to eat their food normally
payload.explanation: Redirecting protest energy into constructive channels like a petition is far more likely to create lasting positive change.

payload.snippet: Leo is on his school bus alone when it unexpectedly breaks down in an unfamiliar rural area far from any buildings with no mobile signal, and the driver is outside assessing the damage leaving Leo entirely on his own inside the vehicle.
options: stays in the bus, does not wander off alone, and waits for the driver to return with a plan
gets out to explore the area and look for help entirely on his own
tries to drive the bus himself since the keys are still in the ignition
walks along the road alone hoping to eventually find a telephone box
payload.explanation: Staying in the bus and waiting for the driver ensures Leo stays safe and is easy to locate.

payload.snippet: Mia is on a city bus when a passenger pulls the emergency alarm and shouts their bag has been stolen, causing panic as passengers rush toward the exits while the bus is still moving.
options: stays seated with her bag held tightly and waits for the bus to stop safely
rushes to the exit doors with everyone else while the bus is still moving
tries to see who stole the bag so she can call out a description
calls emergency services before the bus has even stopped or the driver has responded
payload.explanation: Staying seated until the bus stops safely prevents injury from the moving vehicle.

payload.snippet: Kai is on the school bus when a classmate begins to have what appears to be a severe allergic reaction — face swelling, difficulty breathing — and the teacher supervising is at the very back of the bus and has not yet noticed.
options: shouts clearly to the teacher immediately and describes exactly what he is seeing
runs to get the teacher but this takes more time than simply calling out
waits for the classmate to alert the teacher themselves
gives the classmate water to try to help reduce the swelling on their face
payload.explanation: Shouting to the teacher immediately is faster than physically moving — seconds matter in anaphylaxis.

payload.snippet: Nina is on a bus when she realises a man has been taking photos of her and other young passengers on his phone without permission and has been doing so for several stops.
options: discreetly informs the driver immediately and stays calm and seated
confronts the man loudly and demands he delete the photos immediately
asks the person next to her to confirm what she is seeing before acting
takes photos of the man on her own phone as counter-evidence before doing anything
payload.explanation: Informing the driver immediately and discreetly is safest — confrontation could escalate dangerously.

payload.snippet: Tom is on the school bus when the driver suddenly slumps forward and loses consciousness, with the bus still moving forward on a road with vehicles around it.
options: shouts to alert other passengers and immediately tries to safely apply the handbrake or emergency stop
waits to see if the driver wakes up before taking any action at all
runs to the front and attempts to drive the bus himself toward safety
calls his parents before taking any action to ask them what he should do
payload.explanation: Alerting others and attempting to stop the bus safely is the correct emergency response to driver incapacitation.

payload.snippet: Ava is on the bus during an unexpected severe storm when flash flooding rises rapidly around the vehicle, the engine stalls, and water starts entering through the bottom of the doors.
options: helps passengers move to higher positions in the bus and ensures emergency services are called
opens the bus doors immediately to get everyone out into the rising flood water
stays seated calmly and waits for the water levels to stabilise on their own
tries repeatedly to restart the bus engine in order to drive out of the floodwater
payload.explanation: Moving to higher ground inside the vehicle and calling emergency services is the correct response to vehicle flooding.

payload.snippet: Ben is on the bus when two passengers begin a serious fight and one appears to have a weapon, causing other passengers to panic and run toward his end of the vehicle.
options: stays as low and still as possible, moves away from the conflict area, and calls emergency services
tries to reason with the passengers to calm the situation down himself
shouts instructions to other panicking passengers about what everyone should do
gets off at the very next stop even before the bus has come to a full stop
payload.explanation: Staying low, moving away from danger, and calling emergency services is the correct response.

payload.snippet: Grace is on the bus when she overhears a teenager on the phone arranging a drug deal to happen at a location near her school, giving specific details about the time and place of the exchange.
options: tells a trusted teacher or parent when she arrives at school, sharing the specific details she heard
reports it anonymously online using a crime reporting website straightaway
confronts the teenager on the bus and tells them she overheard everything
says nothing since she cannot be completely certain of what she overheard
payload.explanation: Telling a trusted adult with specific details gives authorities the best chance of preventing harm.

payload.snippet: Max witnesses a physical altercation on the bus that results in an elderly passenger falling and being clearly unable to get up, while other passengers nearby watch but no one takes any action.
options: immediately calls emergency services and tells the driver, then helps keep bystanders back from the injured passenger
attempts to help lift the elderly passenger up from the floor immediately
waits for other older passengers to step forward and take charge of the situation
shouts instructions to bystanders from where he is sitting rather than calling for any help
payload.explanation: Calling emergency services, alerting the driver, and keeping others back is the correct response to a fall injury.

payload.snippet: Lily is on the bus with younger children from her street when she discovers the bus driver has taken a seriously wrong road and is now heading toward a motorway where the bus is not permitted to travel.
options: calmly walks to the driver and clearly informs them of the route error before the motorway entrance
waits and watches to see if the driver realises the mistake before reaching the motorway
tells the children with her that everything will be fine and says nothing to the driver
calls emergency services to report a bus heading the wrong way toward a motorway
payload.explanation: Calmly informing the driver before the motorway is the most effective and proportionate action.

payload.snippet: Zoe is on the bus when a passenger collapses and stops breathing and no other adult passenger is taking action to help.
options: calls emergency services immediately, puts the phone on speaker, and follows the emergency operator's instructions carefully
begins CPR immediately from memory without calling for help first
asks the bus driver to come and help since she does not know what to do herself
checks repeatedly if the person is breathing by shaking them and shouting for help
payload.explanation: Calling emergency services first and following their instructions ensures trained guidance throughout the emergency.

payload.snippet: Sam is on the bus with friends when they collectively decide to record a dangerous stunt video on the moving bus for social media and are pressuring Sam to participate to help get the most views.
options: refuses clearly and explains the serious danger to himself and every other passenger on the bus
participates in a very minor role so his friends do not turn on him
goes along with holding the camera without participating in the stunt itself
reports the plan to the driver before his friends can actually start it
payload.explanation: Refusing clearly and explaining the danger is the most direct and honest way to handle this peer pressure.

payload.snippet: Finn is on the bus when he discovers his friend has been running a scheme where he overcharges younger students for saving them bus seats and pockets the collected money, and asks Finn to help expand the operation.
options: refuses to participate and tells his friend clearly that the scheme is dishonest and must stop
participates for a short time to see how the scheme works before deciding what to do
reports the scheme to school authorities immediately without giving his friend any warning first
agrees to take part only on the condition that all the money is donated to a charity
payload.explanation: Refusing and telling his friend to stop is the honest first step — it gives the friend a chance to end it.

payload.snippet: Ruby is on the bus when extreme fog reduces visibility to near zero and the bus slows significantly, but several passengers are loudly demanding the driver continue at full speed so they are not late.
options: stays quiet and trusts the driver to make the safest speed decision in the conditions
supports the pressuring passengers to help ensure she is not also late to school
asks the driver to pull over completely and stop until the fog clears entirely
moves to the very front of the bus to personally help the driver watch the road ahead
payload.explanation: Supporting the driver by not adding pressure is the safest and most respectful action during difficult driving conditions.

payload.snippet: Isla is on the school bus when she discovers a classmate sitting next to her is carrying something that looks like a weapon in an outer pocket of their bag and appears very distressed and angry.
options: quietly and carefully moves away and immediately tells the driver without alerting the classmate
asks her classmate directly if the item is a weapon and what they plan to do with it
whispers to the students around her so they can all quietly move away together first
calls emergency services immediately from her seat without moving or telling the driver first
payload.explanation: Quietly moving away and alerting the driver minimises risk while getting the right people involved.

payload.snippet: Owen is on the bus late at night when another passenger who has been making everyone uncomfortable suddenly becomes very aggressive toward the driver and physically blocks the exit doors so no one can leave.
options: calls emergency services immediately and stays as calm and still as possible in his seat
joins other passengers in rushing the aggressive person together to clear the exit doors
shouts at the aggressive person loudly to stand down with a group of other passengers
opens a window and calls out for help from passing pedestrians on the street
payload.explanation: Calling emergency services immediately and staying calm is the correct response to a dangerous situation.

payload.snippet: Sophie's friend has taken medication that was not prescribed to them and is now feeling dizzy and very unwell on the moving coach during a long school trip.
options: immediately tells the supervising teacher exactly what happened and what was taken
gives her friend water and waits to see if they recover before telling any adult
texts her friend's parent by message and then waits for instructions to arrive
handles it herself to protect her friend from getting into serious trouble at school
payload.explanation: Telling the supervising teacher immediately with all the details ensures the correct medical response.

payload.snippet: Jake is on the bus when he witnesses a passenger faint, fall, and hit their head on the metal seat edge, losing consciousness with a visible head wound that is bleeding.
options: calls emergency services immediately, keeps the person still, and tells the driver to stop the bus
moves the person immediately to a more comfortable position on the floor
applies pressure to the head wound himself before calling anyone for help
asks other passengers to assess the situation before deciding whether to call for help
payload.explanation: Calling emergency services, keeping the person still, and stopping the bus are the three correct immediate actions for a serious head injury.

payload.snippet: Chloe is on the bus when she notices smoke and a strong burning smell coming from the engine compartment below the vehicle, though the driver has not yet noticed anything wrong.
options: immediately tells the driver clearly and urgently that there is a burning smell from below the bus
opens a window and begins quietly encouraging passengers near her to prepare to exit
waits to see if the driver independently notices and acts since they are more qualified to judge
calls emergency services before alerting the driver to ensure help is already coming
payload.explanation: Alerting the driver immediately is the first correct action — they can stop the bus and initiate the evacuation procedure.

payload.snippet: Ethan is on a school bus that is involved in a collision with another vehicle at a junction, injuring several students, while the shaken driver is conscious but other students are beginning to panic around him.
options: helps calm the students around him, checks they are okay, and confirms emergency services have been called
organises students to start getting off the bus immediately to clear the accident scene
takes charge himself and begins moving injured students to more comfortable positions
calls his parents to come and collect him rather than calling the emergency services himself
payload.explanation: Helping to calm others, staying put to avoid aggravating injuries, and ensuring emergency services are called is the correct approach.

payload.snippet: Leo discovers that a trusted family member has been secretly using his identity to open accounts and take out loans without his knowledge, leaving him responsible for debts he never agreed to.
options: tells his parents immediately and asks them to contact the relevant authorities
says nothing since reporting a family member feels too disloyal
tries to pay off the debts himself by working extra jobs secretly
confronts the family member alone without involving any other adults
payload.explanation: Telling parents and involving authorities is essential — identity theft is a serious crime requiring formal action.

payload.snippet: Mia is approached at school by a stranger who asks her to carry a bag of cash across town for cash in hand, claiming it is completely legal and very simple.
options: refuses firmly and tells a teacher or parent about the approach immediately
accepts the job since it sounds straightforward and she needs the money
asks what is inside the bag before deciding whether to accept the job
refuses but does not tell any adult about the suspicious approach
payload.explanation: Refusing and telling an adult is the correct response — being used to move cash for unknown purposes can involve criminal activity.

payload.snippet: Kai is part of a group of friends who discover a large sum of cash in an abandoned bag and immediately begin arguing about what to do with it.
options: advocates strongly for handing it in to the police as lost property
suggests splitting it equally since it seems like no one will claim it
takes his share quietly before anyone has agreed what to do
leaves the whole decision to his friends and whatever they decide
payload.explanation: Handing cash to the police is the legally correct action — keeping found property of significant value is theft.

payload.snippet: Nina is offered a part-time job that pays unusually well but requires her to work off the books with no contract and no record of her income.
options: declines and explains she needs a proper contract and record of income
accepts because the high pay outweighs the lack of formal arrangement
accepts for a short time to see if it is legitimate before deciding
accepts and tells no one about the arrangement since it feels secretive
payload.explanation: Declining an uncontracted cash-in-hand job protects her from potential exploitation and legal issues.

payload.snippet: Tom's friend group wants to pool their money together to buy something expensive from someone online, but only one friend has actually seen any evidence that the seller exists.
options: suggests the group wait until the seller's legitimacy is properly confirmed
puts money in immediately since all his friends are doing it
puts in a very small amount to test whether the seller is genuine
refuses to join the group purchase but says nothing about his concern to the others
payload.explanation: Waiting for verified legitimacy before committing money prevents potential group financial fraud.

payload.snippet: Ava discovers that an adult family friend has been slowly taking small amounts of money from her elderly grandparent over many months and the grandparent does not fully understand what has been happening.
options: tells her parents immediately about what she has discovered
confronts the adult family friend alone and demands they stop
says nothing since she is not fully certain and does not want to cause upset
tells her grandparent directly hoping they will take action themselves
payload.explanation: Telling parents immediately about suspected elder financial abuse is the correct and urgent action.

payload.snippet: Ben is offered a large sum of money to stay quiet about something genuinely wrong that he has witnessed involving people he trusts.
options: refuses the money and still does the right thing by speaking to a trusted adult
takes the money since the amount would significantly help his family
takes the money but tells someone anyway feeling the offer itself was wrong
refuses the money but also stays quiet since speaking up seems too risky
payload.explanation: Refusing a bribe and still reporting the wrongdoing is the morally correct and legally important action.

payload.snippet: Grace is running the school charity account and receives a message from what appears to be the school's official email account asking her to transfer money to a new account.
options: does not transfer anything and speaks to the teacher in person to verify the request
transfers the money since the email appears to come from the school
emails back to ask more questions before deciding whether to transfer
transfers a small test amount to see if the account is real first
payload.explanation: Never transferring money based solely on an email — always verify in person. This is a common fraud pattern.

payload.snippet: Max finds out that a popular social media influencer he trusted has been paid to promote a financial product that experts say is highly risky and misleading.
options: researches the product independently and warns his friends not to act on the influencer's advice
invests in the product since the influencer has never misled him before
partially invests while also researching independently to be careful
ignores the information since the influencer probably did not know the product was misleading
payload.explanation: Independent research and warning friends is the responsible response to potentially misleading financial advice.

payload.snippet: Lily is running a genuine fundraiser but discovers a classmate has started a fake copycat fundraiser online using the same cause to keep the donations for themselves.
options: tells a trusted adult and helps the school report the fake fundraiser
launches a public campaign against her classmate exposing them online
ignores it since she cannot prove the fundraiser is definitely fake
contacts the fundraising platform directly herself to report the account
payload.explanation: Involving a trusted adult to formally report the fake fundraiser is the correct and proportionate response.

payload.snippet: Zoe discovers her older sibling has taken out a very large informal loan from a local moneylender at extremely high interest rates and is now struggling to repay it.
options: encourages her sibling to speak to their parents and seek help from a citizens advice service
lends her sibling all her savings to help pay off the debt immediately
tells her parents without her sibling's knowledge hoping they will help
stays out of it entirely since her sibling is old enough to manage their own finances
payload.explanation: Encouraging the sibling to seek proper advice from support services is more sustainable than informal help.

payload.snippet: Sam is running a school business project and his team discovers that the most profitable strategy involves misleading customers about what the product actually does.
options: refuses to mislead customers and suggests finding an honest competitive advantage instead
goes along with the strategy since it is only a school project and not real
uses the strategy but in a mild way hoping it still counts as acceptable
leaves the team rather than continuing but says nothing about why he left
payload.explanation: Refusing and redirecting to an honest strategy is both the ethical and legally correct approach.

payload.snippet: Finn is pressured by friends to join a pyramid investment scheme where the first people to join will profit massively from those who join later.
options: explains why pyramid schemes are mathematically harmful and refuses to join or recruit others
joins at the top level since he would be among the first to profit
joins at a lower level to see how it works before deciding to recruit anyone
refuses to join but does not explain to his friends why the scheme is harmful
payload.explanation: Understanding and refusing pyramid schemes — and explaining why — protects both Finn and his friends.

payload.snippet: Ruby is offered shares in a startup by a family friend who says the company is guaranteed to succeed and wants her to put in all her savings before the offer expires tonight.
options: declines firmly and explains she never makes financial decisions under artificial time pressure
invests a small amount to avoid disappointing the family friend
invests everything since the family friend would not lie to her
asks her parents that evening and invests if they agree, not noticing the pressure tactic
payload.explanation: Recognising and refusing high-pressure time-limited investment offers is a critical financial safety skill.

payload.snippet: Owen witnesses a teacher at his school accepting money from a parent in exchange for giving their child better grades, and several other students seem to know about it.
options: tells a trusted senior staff member or parent about what he witnessed
stays quiet since reporting a teacher feels extremely risky and frightening
tells as many students as possible to expose the teacher quickly
confronts the teacher directly asking them to stop the arrangement
payload.explanation: Reporting to a senior staff member is the correct and safe action — academic corruption affects all students fairly.

payload.snippet: Sophie is running a group holiday fund with friends and discovers that the person collecting the money has been spending small amounts on personal items, telling herself she will replace them.
options: raises the issue with the whole group calmly and asks that the records be reviewed
says nothing since the person is her close friend and might just be temporarily borrowing
confronts the person alone hoping to resolve it without involving the others
removes herself from the holiday fund and refuses to explain why she is leaving
payload.explanation: Raising the issue with the whole group and reviewing records ensures transparency and fairness.

payload.snippet: Jake discovers a vulnerability in a school payment system that would allow him to add credit to his account without paying, and a friend dares him to try it.
options: reports the vulnerability to the school IT team immediately without using it
tries it once to see if it works before reporting it
reports it only after his friend tries it first to confirm it works
uses it just a small amount and then reports it claiming he found it by accident
payload.explanation: Reporting a financial system vulnerability without exploiting it is both honest and legally responsible.

payload.snippet: Chloe finds out that a charity she has been fundraising for has been operating fraudulently and none of the money collected has gone to the stated cause.
options: contacts the relevant charity regulator to report what she has discovered
posts about it on social media immediately to warn all potential donors
stops fundraising quietly without telling anyone why
confronts the charity organisers directly and demands they explain themselves
payload.explanation: Contacting the official charity regulator is the correct and most impactful formal response to charity fraud.

payload.snippet: Ethan is approached by someone online claiming to be from his bank, saying his account has been compromised and asking him to confirm his card number and PIN to protect his funds.
options: closes the communication and contacts his bank directly using the number on his card
gives the information since it appears urgent and his bank needs to protect his money
gives only some information thinking partial details will be enough to verify his identity
calls the number provided in the message to check whether the communication is genuine
payload.explanation: Closing suspicious communications and contacting the bank independently is the correct response to a phishing attempt.

payload.snippet: Isla realises the small community fundraiser she organised has collected far more money than the original target and people are now asking whether she can pocket the surplus.
options: holds a meeting to decide democratically what to do with the surplus
keeps the surplus since she did all the organising work and deserves it
donates it to a related cause without consulting the donors first
returns it proportionally to every single donor which takes enormous effort
payload.explanation: A democratic decision about the surplus respects all contributors and ensures transparent, fair use of the funds.

payload.snippet: Leo is hiking alone in a remote area when he is bitten by a snake he cannot identify, and his mobile phone has no signal and the nearest road is two hours away on foot.
options: stays calm, immobilises the bitten limb below heart level, marks the bite site, and begins walking slowly toward help
sucks the venom out of the bite wound immediately using his mouth
runs as fast as possible toward the road to reach help as quickly as possible
cuts across the bite wound with his penknife to drain the venom from the wound
payload.explanation: Immobilising the limb, staying calm, and moving slowly toward help is correct — sucking, cutting, and running all accelerate venom spread.

payload.snippet: Mia is scuba diving in a coral reef when her underwater camera strobe accidentally fires directly into the eyes of a large resting shark, which immediately becomes agitated and circles her.
options: stops all movement completely, descends slightly, and waits for the shark to calm before ascending slowly with a buddy
swims to the surface as fast as possible to get out of the water immediately
drives the shark away by pushing it firmly on the snout with both hands
uses her tank to make bubbles aggressively to try to scare the shark away
payload.explanation: Staying still and calm is critical — rapid ascent risks decompression sickness, and aggressive action can provoke a shark.

payload.snippet: Kai is leading a group of younger children on a school nature walk when they encounter a large cow with a calf that moves aggressively between the group and the exit gate.
options: calmly walks the children around the perimeter of the field toward the boundary fence
leads the group directly past the cow and calf at a brisk pace to reach the gate
makes loud noise to drive the cow toward the far end of the field first
tells the children to spread out so the cow cannot target the whole group at once
payload.explanation: Moving around the perimeter away from the calf is safest — cows with calves are extremely protective of the direct path to their young.

payload.snippet: Nina is on a conservation volunteer trip in Africa when she sees a poacher setting an illegal snare in the park during a guided walk, and the poacher notices that she has seen him.
options: stays calm, makes no sudden moves, and tells the guide as discreetly and immediately as possible
photographs the poacher quickly on her phone while he can see her doing it
confronts the poacher and tells him she has seen what he is doing and will report it
says nothing and looks away to avoid any potential confrontation with the poacher
payload.explanation: Alerting the guide immediately and discreetly is the safest action — confronting an illegal poacher is genuinely dangerous.

payload.snippet: Tom is at a wildlife sanctuary when a large primate escapes its enclosure and is spotted in the area where school visitors are walking.
options: gathers the nearest children, moves calmly away from the primate, and alerts sanctuary staff immediately
stays still and makes eye contact with the primate to show he is not a threat
makes gentle soothing sounds and crouches down to appear smaller and less threatening
climbs a nearby structure to get above the primate's line of sight quickly
payload.explanation: Moving calmly away and alerting staff is the correct action — eye contact can be interpreted as a threat by primates.

payload.snippet: Ava is on a kayaking expedition in an estuary when a large pod of dolphins surrounds her group and begins surfing the kayak bow waves, making it impossible to paddle without potentially hitting them.
options: stops paddling completely and lets the kayaks drift until the dolphins move on naturally
paddles gently through the pod trying to minimise contact with the animals
bangs the side of the kayak to encourage the dolphins to give the group more space
paddles hard to speed up and exit the dolphin pod as quickly as possible
payload.explanation: Stopping and drifting is the correct response — dolphins choose to interact on their terms and will move on when ready.

payload.snippet: Ben is on a research vessel when a massive sea turtle becomes tangled in trailing fishing rope from the boat and the captain asks for volunteers to free it before it drowns.
options: puts on a life jacket and assists the trained crew member who is already managing the rope
dives into the water immediately without equipment to start cutting the rope himself
leans over the side of the boat and cuts the rope nearest the boat first to release tension
tells the captain the turtle should be pulled onto the boat to be freed more easily
payload.explanation: Assisting the trained crew member safely is correct — diving in alone without equipment or training creates additional danger.

payload.snippet: Grace is staying at a remote farmhouse when the family dog begins barking urgently at a specific spot near the barn wall during the night, and when she investigates she finds a large slow-moving creature she cannot identify.
options: goes back inside, tells the adults in the house, and lets them investigate with a torch and appropriate equipment
stays outside to shine her phone light at the creature and film it for identification
tries to move the creature herself to get it away from the barn before waking the adults
shouts to wake the adults from outside the window describing the situation loudly
payload.explanation: Going inside and alerting the adults with better equipment and experience is the safest and most sensible action.

payload.snippet: Max finds a whale that has beached itself on a quiet stretch of coastline with no other people visible and the whale appears to be alive but very distressed.
options: calls the emergency services and the national cetacean rescue organisation immediately, keeping the whale wet if possible by gently splashing water
tries to push the whale back into the water himself to save its life immediately
covers the whale with wet sand to keep it moist and waits without calling anyone
calls only his parents and lets them decide what to do while the whale lies there
payload.explanation: Calling emergency services and the cetacean rescue organisation is the correct action — pushing a whale alone can kill it, and specialists are needed.

payload.snippet: Lily is hiking when she discovers an illegal animal trap that has caught a large wild mammal in extreme distress, and the animal is clearly badly injured and dangerous.
options: marks the location clearly, calls animal welfare services and police, and keeps a safe distance
attempts to free the animal herself by releasing the trap mechanism
calls only animal welfare but not police since it is a welfare not criminal matter
tries to approach the animal slowly to assess the extent of the injury closely
payload.explanation: Marking the location, calling both animal welfare and police, and staying at a safe distance is the correct multi-agency response.

payload.snippet: Zoe is volunteering at an animal rehabilitation centre when a large injured raptor she is helping to treat breaks free inside a small room and begins striking at her with its talons.
options: presses herself flat against the wall, uses her thick arm covering as a shield, and calls for help
runs out of the room slamming the door which may further panic the bird
tries to grab the bird's wings to control it and prevent further damage to the room
ducks and covers her head waiting for the bird to calm down on its own
payload.explanation: Pressing against the wall using protective covering and calling for help is the safest response — running or grabbing can cause serious injury.

payload.snippet: Sam is on a marine biology field trip when a fellow student accidentally steps on and becomes entangled with a large venomous sea creature, and the student is beginning to show symptoms of a reaction.
options: calls the supervising teacher and emergency services immediately and keeps the student calm and still
tries to identify the exact species by searching his notes to determine the correct antidote
helps remove the tentacles or spines himself using bare hands as quickly as possible
gives the student antihistamine tablets from the first aid kit since it appears to be an allergic reaction
payload.explanation: Calling for expert emergency help immediately is the only correct response — identification and treatment require medical professionals.

payload.snippet: Finn is in a remote area when his group encounters a pack of wolves moving through the trees toward them and the group leader is at the back of the party and has not yet noticed.
options: calmly and quietly moves to alert the group leader while keeping the group together in a cluster
shouts to the group leader from the front causing sudden loud noise near the wolves
waves his arms large and wide so the wolves can see the full human group size immediately
climbs the nearest tall tree quickly and calls down instructions to the rest of the group
payload.explanation: Quietly alerting the leader while keeping the group clustered together is the correct response — loud sudden noise and sudden movement near wolves increases risk.

payload.snippet: Ruby is on a conservation expedition when she discovers a critically endangered animal that has never been officially documented in that region, but photographing or reporting it could attract illegal poachers to the area.
options: discusses the discovery only with the lead conservation scientist on the expedition privately
posts the discovery on social media immediately since it is a remarkable find for science
photographs the animal extensively before reporting it to ensure documentation is thorough
reports it immediately to every conservation organisation she knows at the same time
payload.explanation: Reporting privately to the lead conservation scientist protects the animal while ensuring the discovery is handled with expertise.

payload.snippet: Owen is assisting a vet when the vet is suddenly rendered unconscious during a procedure on a large animal and the animal is mid-procedure and showing signs of pain and distress.
options: keeps the animal as still and calm as possible and calls for emergency veterinary assistance immediately
continues the procedure himself following the steps he observed the vet beginning
leaves the animal and runs to find the nearest available adult regardless of their qualifications
administers additional sedation from the labelled bottles on the table to reduce the animal's distress
payload.explanation: Keeping the animal calm and calling for qualified veterinary help immediately is the only correct response — administering unknown doses without training could be fatal.

payload.snippet: Sophie is leading an eco-tourism kayaking group when a member of the public on a speedboat deliberately drives aggressively close to a pod of dolphins the group is respectfully observing from distance.
options: records the speedboat registration, calls the coastguard, and reports the harassment to marine wildlife authorities
paddles her kayak between the speedboat and the dolphins to protect the pod
shouts loudly at the speedboat operator to make them aware of the dolphins
takes the group away from the area immediately without reporting the incident
payload.explanation: Recording and reporting to the coastguard and marine wildlife authorities creates a formal record and enables enforcement action.

payload.snippet: Jake discovers a large illegal wildlife trafficking operation at a local market while on a school trip abroad, with clearly distressed animals being sold in poor conditions.
options: memorises key details, tells the school trip supervisor immediately, and lets adults contact local authorities
films everything on his phone and posts it directly to international wildlife protection accounts
confronts the market traders directly to demand they release the animals
tells only his school friends so they can all report it independently to different organisations
payload.explanation: Telling the supervisor and letting adults contact the proper authorities is the safest and most effective action in an unfamiliar country.

payload.snippet: Chloe is working on a marine reserve when a massive bloom of toxic algae appears overnight in a bay where children's swimming activities are planned for the next morning.
options: reports it immediately to the reserve manager and marine authorities so the swimming can be cancelled
tests the water herself using the basic water testing kit on the boat
posts on the reserve social media page warning families not to swim tomorrow morning
waits until morning to see if the bloom has dispersed naturally before raising an alarm
payload.explanation: Reporting immediately to the reserve manager ensures the swimming is officially cancelled through the correct safety channels.

payload.snippet: Ethan is on a research trip when the expedition scientist asks him to handle a legally protected species in a way that would technically violate wildlife law, claiming it is for science and will not matter.
options: politely declines and raises his concern about the legal status of the proposed handling
follows the scientist's instructions since the scientist has more authority than the law
handles the animal as asked but reports the scientist to authorities after returning home
refuses without explanation and walks away from the situation entirely
payload.explanation: Politely declining and raising the legal concern immediately is the correct and professional action.

payload.snippet: Isla witnesses a professional wildlife photographer deliberately disturbing a nesting osprey to get a better shot, which is a specific protected offence in the country they are in.
options: reports the photographer to the relevant wildlife protection authority with the photographer's details and location
confronts the photographer and demands they leave the nesting site immediately
films the photographer from a distance as evidence and posts it to online wildlife communities
tells the nature reserve office when she returns without providing identifying details of the photographer
payload.explanation: Reporting with full details to the wildlife protection authority enables formal enforcement and prosecution if warranted.

payload.snippet: Leo is a young engineer attending a planning meeting where a proposed tall building will permanently block daylight to the social housing block next door, and the planning officer appears to have not noticed this in the assessment.
options: raises the daylight impact formally during the public comment section of the meeting with supporting evidence
stays quiet since raising it might embarrass the planning officer publicly
privately tells the affected residents after the meeting so they can object themselves
refuses to attend any more planning meetings in protest at the oversight
payload.explanation: Raising it formally during the public comment section is both the correct procedure and the most effective way to get it into the official record.

payload.snippet: Mia is working as a junior engineer at a firm when she discovers that the cost-cutting changes made to a major public building's fire suppression system may render it non-compliant with safety standards.
options: documents the concern formally and escalates through official channels, including the building control authority if needed
asks her manager about it informally and accepts whatever explanation is given
tells her colleagues but not her manager since she is too junior to raise it officially
leaves the company without raising the concern to protect herself from retaliation
payload.explanation: Fire safety non-compliance in public buildings requires formal escalation — including to regulators if internal channels fail.

payload.snippet: Kai is at a community consultation about a planned factory development when he realises the environmental impact assessment does not address the effect on the local river's salmon habitat.
options: speaks at the consultation to raise the omission formally and requests a supplementary assessment
contacts an environmental law group after the consultation to request a judicial review
organises a community petition which will carry more weight than a single individual's comment
says nothing at the meeting but sends a detailed letter to the planning authority afterwards
payload.explanation: Raising the omission formally during the consultation creates an official record — all three approaches have merit and can be combined.

payload.snippet: Nina discovers that a residential developer has been falsifying soil contamination test results to speed up planning approval for a housing development on a former industrial site.
options: reports the falsification to the relevant environmental regulator with any evidence she has access to
contacts the local newspaper so the story is made public before the approval is granted
tells the planning authority without providing evidence since they can investigate themselves
raises it at the planning meeting and challenges the developer directly in front of everyone
payload.explanation: Reporting to the regulator with evidence triggers a formal investigation and is the most likely course of action to stop an unsafe development.

payload.snippet: Tom is doing community service helping restore a historic bridge when he discovers the surveyor's assessment was based on incomplete data and the bridge may be less safe than certified.
options: tells the project manager and suggests the survey is redone before restoration continues
completes his volunteering shift as normal since he is not a qualified engineer
stops working and tells other volunteers to also stop until the issue is resolved
emails the heritage authority directly without informing the project manager first
payload.explanation: Telling the project manager immediately gives the person with authority the chance to act — stopping work unilaterally could create its own problems.

payload.snippet: Ava's school design competition requires students to design a community centre for a neighbourhood they have no personal experience of, and she discovers the brief assumes all residents have cars.
options: researches the actual transport patterns of the neighbourhood before designing
designs for car-owning users since that is what the brief specifies even if it seems wrong
adds a note to her design pointing out the assumption without changing the design itself
contacts the competition organisers to challenge the brief before submitting her design
payload.explanation: Researching actual conditions produces a genuinely useful design — challenging the brief with evidence is also valid, making both options appropriate.

payload.snippet: Ben discovers that a structural wall in his school building shows signs of significant movement that could indicate subsidence, but when he reports it the caretaker dismisses it as normal settling.
options: tells a teacher or member of senior leadership directly and formally as well
accepts the caretaker's expert opinion and says nothing further about it
tells his parents and asks them to contact the school formally on his behalf
takes photos of the cracks and posts them on social media to pressure the school to act
payload.explanation: Escalating to senior leadership when a safety concern is dismissed by a caretaker ensures the right people make the decision.

payload.snippet: Grace is participating in a design-build challenge when she realises the materials provided to all teams are significantly weaker than specified in the challenge rules.
options: raises the discrepancy with the challenge organisers before beginning so all teams are equally informed
uses the weak materials since every team has the same materials and the playing field is level
sources her own stronger materials from outside the challenge to give her team an advantage
tells only her own team about the weakness and uses this knowledge to design around it
payload.explanation: Raising the discrepancy before starting ensures all teams compete on the same informed basis.

payload.snippet: Max is volunteering at a social housing building project when a more experienced volunteer shows him a much faster construction method that skips a specific insulation step.
options: asks whether skipping the insulation step meets the building code before agreeing to use the method
uses the faster method since the experienced volunteer clearly knows more than him
refuses to use the faster method without explanation and continues as originally trained
uses the faster method for the external walls but keeps the correct method for internal walls
payload.explanation: Checking whether a shortcut meets building code is the correct question before any change in method on a residential building.

payload.snippet: Lily is designing an inclusive school building for a design project and discovers that universal design standards conflict with heritage preservation requirements for the existing building shell.
options: presents both sets of requirements honestly in her design and explains the trade-off clearly
prioritises heritage since the school is famous and many people would oppose changes to the appearance
prioritises accessibility since current pupils have legal rights that outweigh historical considerations
asks the design teacher whether heritage or accessibility should take priority before proceeding
payload.explanation: Presenting both sets of requirements honestly and explaining the trade-off shows design maturity — the trade-off conversation itself is the most important professional skill here.

payload.snippet: Zoe is on a school trip to a construction site when she sees a worker operating machinery without the correct safety certification visible on their hard hat.
options: reports what she observed to the site safety officer after the tour
tells the worker directly that they appear to be missing their certification badge
tells her teacher during the trip so the teacher can raise it with the site manager
says nothing since she could be misreading or misunderstanding what the certification badge looks like
payload.explanation: Reporting to the site safety officer after the tour is the formal and correct channel for a safety observation.

payload.snippet: Sam discovers that his local council has approved planning permission for a development by making a procedural error that allowed them to skip the normal public consultation stage.
options: contacts a local councillor and planning law advice service about the error
accepts the outcome since planning decisions once made are very difficult to reverse
organises a large community protest outside the council offices immediately
writes a letter to the local newspaper exposing the procedural failure publicly
payload.explanation: Contacting a councillor and legal advice service enables a formal challenge through the correct process.

payload.snippet: Finn is on work experience at an engineering firm and discovers that a colleague has been receiving payments from a construction contractor for recommending that firm for work.
options: tells a senior manager about what he has discovered as soon as possible
stays quiet since he is only a work experience student and the colleague is very senior
tells the colleague that he knows about the payments and watches to see what they do
contacts the contractor directly to understand whether the payments were legitimate
payload.explanation: Telling a senior manager immediately is the correct response to suspected corruption — work experience status does not reduce the ethical obligation.

payload.snippet: Ruby is designing an urban park for a class project and discovers that the only available site is on contaminated former industrial land, but the contamination data is incomplete.
options: states clearly in her design report that remediation must be confirmed before any building begins
designs the park anyway using raised planters to avoid contact with the ground soil
leaves the contamination concern out of her report to avoid overcomplicating the design submission
contacts the local environmental agency herself to request the missing contamination data
payload.explanation: Stating the precondition clearly in the report is the professional and honest approach — it protects her design from being used without appropriate remediation.

payload.snippet: Owen is leading a school team building a community bee garden when a corporate sponsor asks to put a very large brand logo on the central structure, which would dominate the natural space.
options: presents the concern to the team and to the project coordinator before responding to the sponsor
accepts the logo since the sponsor has funded the project and has the right to brand it
rejects the logo independently and thanks the sponsor but removes their involvement
suggests a much smaller logo on a discreet entry sign as a compromise to the sponsor
payload.explanation: Presenting the concern to the team and coordinator involves all stakeholders before a decision is made.

payload.snippet: Sophie witnesses a construction worker at a building site adjacent to her school being pressured by a supervisor to work on scaffolding in unsafe conditions during strong winds.
options: reports what she saw to her school and suggests they contact the Health and Safety Executive
approaches the supervisor directly at the boundary fence and tells them to stop
takes a photo and posts it online tagging the building company's account
tells her school but only as a general observation without urging any formal action
payload.explanation: Reporting with a suggestion to contact the HSE creates the most formal and protective response — the HSE has enforcement powers.

payload.snippet: Jake is part of a community self-build housing scheme and the group must decide whether to use a faster building method that will reduce energy efficiency by a significant margin.
options: proposes commissioning an independent assessment of the long-term cost and carbon impact before deciding
supports the faster method since the community needs the houses completed soon
opposes the faster method on environmental grounds without quantifying the actual impact
lets the majority vote decide without adding any technical analysis to the discussion
payload.explanation: An independent assessment of long-term costs and carbon impact gives the decision the evidence base it needs.

payload.snippet: Chloe is helping plan a public building and discovers that the lead architect has specified a type of cladding that is similar to one implicated in a serious building fire in another country.
options: raises the cladding concern with the project manager and requests a fire safety review of the specification
assumes the architect has already reviewed the fire safety data since they are qualified
tells a local journalist about the specification since public scrutiny may pressure a change
researches the cladding type herself and makes her own risk assessment before escalating
payload.explanation: Raising the concern with the project manager and requesting a formal fire safety review is the correct and proportionate professional response.

payload.snippet: Ethan is designing social housing as part of a school architecture project when he discovers that the density required by the brief will make it impossible to include any communal green space.
options: challenges the density requirement in his design narrative and proposes a viable alternative
designs to the density specified and includes no green space as the brief effectively requires
reduces the density to include green space but does not explain the departure from the brief
tells his teacher the brief is flawed and asks for a modified brief before proceeding
payload.explanation: Challenging the requirement in the design narrative while proposing an alternative is the most professionally complete response.

payload.snippet: Isla discovers that a major infrastructure project that will benefit her city has been approved using a financial model that appears to have significantly underestimated the long-term maintenance costs.
options: writes a detailed and evidenced submission to the relevant scrutiny committee
accepts that infrastructure decisions are made by qualified experts who have reviewed the numbers
organises a public awareness campaign before the scrutiny committee has reviewed it
sends her analysis to the project's lead engineer directly for comment
payload.explanation: A detailed evidenced submission to a scrutiny committee is the correct formal democratic channel for raising concerns about public infrastructure finance.

payload.snippet: Leo discovers a manuscript in his school library's archive that appears to be an unpublished work by a significant historical author, and the school does not seem to know it exists.
options: tells the school librarian immediately and suggests they contact a literary archivist or university
photographs every page himself and publishes the manuscript online so scholars can access it
borrows the manuscript to read at home before deciding what to do with the discovery
keeps the discovery to himself while he researches the author further
payload.explanation: Telling the librarian and suggesting expert contact is the correct first step — the manuscript must stay in safe institutional hands.

payload.snippet: Mia's creative writing piece for a national competition has been plagiarised in full by another entrant who has submitted it under their own name.
options: reports the plagiarism to the competition organisers with full evidence of her original authorship
withdraws her own entry in frustration and gives up on the competition
contacts the other entrant privately asking them to withdraw their submission
posts about the plagiarism publicly on social media before the competition has ruled on it
payload.explanation: Reporting to the organisers with evidence is the correct formal channel — public accusations before investigation can create legal risk.

payload.snippet: Kai is editing the school literary magazine when he discovers that an anonymous submission contains what he believes is a fictional retelling of a recent real-world tragedy that affected several students in the school.
options: shows the piece to the teacher supervising the magazine before making any publication decision
publishes it since it is anonymous fiction and no one can prove the connection
rejects it without consulting anyone and tells the author it is not suitable for the magazine
edits the most recognisable details and publishes the edited version
payload.explanation: The teacher must be involved in any publication decision about potentially triggering content that may affect specific students.

payload.snippet: Nina finds a first edition of an extremely valuable book hidden in a box of donated books at the school fair and realises it is worth a very large sum of money.
options: tells the school immediately so the book can be handled correctly and the donor can be contacted
buys the book at the jumble sale price before anyone else notices its value
keeps the book safe but says nothing until she can research its value more carefully
contacts a rare book dealer herself to assess the value before telling the school
payload.explanation: Telling the school immediately is the only honest course — purchasing or withholding information about it could be fraud.

payload.snippet: Tom is invited to contribute to a significant public literary anthology and discovers that one of the other contributors has a history of using their platform to spread harmful ideas.
options: discusses his concern with a trusted adult mentor before deciding how to respond to the invitation
declines the invitation immediately without engaging with the issue further
accepts the invitation and plans to use his contribution to challenge the harmful contributor's ideas
contacts the anthology editor to ask how they handle contributors with controversial public views
payload.explanation: Discussing with a mentor before deciding is the most considered approach — both declining and accepting while engaging are defensible choices.

payload.snippet: Ava is part of a school literary festival committee when she discovers that the headline author invited has recently been involved in a serious controversy that many in the school community find deeply offensive.
options: raises the concern formally with the committee and the supervising teacher before any public action
contacts the author directly to ask them to withdraw from the festival themselves
starts a student campaign to have the author uninvited before the committee has discussed it
says nothing since it is not her decision and the committee adults will deal with it
payload.explanation: Raising the concern formally with the committee and teacher before external action is the correct governance approach.

payload.snippet: Ben is helping a younger student from a difficult home background write a story and realises the story contains detailed, specific information about what may be serious ongoing harm at home.
options: immediately tells the school's designated safeguarding lead about what the student has written
discusses the story calmly with the student to understand how much is real versus fictional
continues the mentoring session normally and reports after the session has fully ended
tells the student's form tutor rather than the designated safeguarding lead since they know the student better
payload.explanation: Telling the designated safeguarding lead immediately is the legal requirement — do not investigate the situation yourself.

payload.snippet: Grace is a young author attending a publishing event when an adult industry professional offers to help her career in exchange for her keeping quiet about something she has just witnessed them do that was wrong.
options: refuses, ends the conversation, and tells a trusted adult about both the offer and what she witnessed
stays quiet about what she saw since her career opportunity feels important right now
tells only her parents about the incident and asks them to decide what to do
reports only what she witnessed, not the offer made to silence her, to keep things simpler
payload.explanation: Refusing the offer and reporting both the original incident and the attempt to silence her is the complete and correct response.

payload.snippet: Max is writing a serialised story online that has unexpectedly attracted a large teenage audience and he realises one chapter he has already planned will contain content that may be harmful to vulnerable young readers.
options: revises the planned chapter to achieve the story's purpose without the potentially harmful elements
publishes the chapter as planned since he has the right to tell the story as he envisioned it
skips the chapter entirely with no explanation and jumps to the next part of the story
adds a warning at the beginning of the chapter and publishes it unchanged
payload.explanation: Revising to achieve the story's purpose without potentially harmful elements is the responsible and creative solution.

payload.snippet: Lily discovers that an entire genre of books she loves has systematically excluded and misrepresented authors from her own cultural background for decades.
options: writes and publicly submits an essay about the systemic exclusion drawing on evidence and research
stops reading that genre entirely as a personal boycott of the publishing industry
starts a social media campaign targeting specific publishers for immediate change
accepts that change is unlikely and focuses on finding the few books in the genre that do include her community
payload.explanation: A well-researched public essay contributes meaningfully to the discourse about systemic publishing inequality.

payload.snippet: Zoe is entering a prestigious creative writing competition when she discovers that the judging panel lacks diversity and their past choices have overwhelmingly favoured a single style of writing.
options: submits her entry in her authentic voice and, if unsuccessful, writes about the pattern she observed
does not enter since the lack of diversity makes a fair outcome unlikely for her
changes her writing style to match what the judges have historically preferred
contacts the competition organisers before entering to challenge the composition of the panel
payload.explanation: Entering in your authentic voice and then writing about observed patterns if unsuccessful is both brave and constructive.

payload.snippet: Sam's published school novel project is discovered to contain a passage that closely mirrors a passage from a lesser-known published author who was never credited.
options: contacts the school and the original author immediately to acknowledge the similarity and apologise
removes the passage from all available copies without acknowledging the issue publicly
claims the similarity is coincidental since the original author is not widely known
asks a teacher to handle the situation so he does not have to address it directly
payload.explanation: Acknowledging the similarity and contacting the original author directly shows integrity and is the correct response to unintentional plagiarism.

payload.snippet: Finn has written a personally significant story about his experience of a mental health crisis that an author-in-residence suggests submitting to a national publication.
options: discusses with a trusted adult the potential benefits and risks of very public personal disclosure before deciding
submits the story immediately since sharing it widely feels like a way to help others
refuses to submit it since publishing something so personal feels too frightening
asks the author-in-residence to submit it on his behalf so he stays at one remove from the decision
payload.explanation: Discussing risks and benefits with a trusted adult before publicly sharing highly personal material is the wise first step.

payload.snippet: Ruby is a published young author who is asked by a major publishing company to write a book that significantly changes her original vision in order to make it more commercially appealing.
options: asks for time to evaluate whether the changes are compatible with what she wants to say
accepts all the changes since the publishing company knows the market better than she does
rejects the deal entirely rather than compromise on any aspect of her original vision
agrees publicly but plans to restore her original vision in the next book
payload.explanation: Asking for time to evaluate ensures she makes the decision from a considered position rather than pressure or impulse.

payload.snippet: Owen is a teenage author whose first book has been criticised in a national review for containing politically charged content that some find offensive.
options: reads the review carefully and responds publicly with a thoughtful and evidence-based reply if he disagrees
ignores all criticism entirely and refuses to engage with any negative reviews
publicly attacks the reviewer on social media for their interpretation of his work
immediately rewrites the relevant sections to remove the content that caused offence
payload.explanation: A thoughtful, evidence-based public reply is the professional and intellectually honest way to engage with criticism.

payload.snippet: Sophie is in a school debate about whether books featuring dark or difficult themes should be permitted in a school library for young readers.
options: argues using specific examples that age-appropriate difficult content helps young people develop empathy and understanding
argues for complete removal of all dark content from school libraries for simplicity
argues that all content should be available with no restrictions in school libraries
refuses to take a clear position since both sides have good points
payload.explanation: A specific, evidence-based argument about the value of age-appropriate difficult content is the most defensible and nuanced position.

payload.snippet: Jake is invited to speak at a literary festival but discovers the festival is sponsored by a company whose practices he considers to be unethical.
options: investigates the nature of the sponsorship and discusses the conflict with a mentor before deciding
declines the invitation immediately without researching the extent of the sponsor's involvement
accepts the invitation and plans to use his speech to critique the sponsor publicly
accepts the invitation and says nothing about the sponsorship since the literary content is separate
payload.explanation: Investigating the details and discussing with a mentor gives him the information he needs to make an informed decision.

payload.snippet: Chloe discovers that a school reading programme designed to help struggling readers is using books that contain content that may inadvertently stigmatise the very students it is trying to help.
options: raises this observation with the teacher running the programme with specific examples
replaces the books herself with ones she considers more appropriate
tells the struggling readers directly about the content so they can make their own choices
reports the programme to the head teacher for immediate review
payload.explanation: Raising specific examples with the teacher running the programme is the direct, evidence-based, and appropriately scaled first action.
